key_insight: CoFINN embeds finite-volume conservation laws into CNN training so flow predictions stay physically consistent, not just visually accurate.
engineering_relevance: This makes neural surrogates more reliable for compressible aerodynamics, especially when shocks and sparse data make standard data-driven models fail.
method: Treats CNN outputs as structured finite-volume grids.
Computes conservation losses using numerical fluxes across cell faces.
Trains on physics-consistent flux balance instead of only pixel-wise error.
evidence_signal: On transonic airfoil cases at M=0.7 and Re=6×10^6, the method reduced drag prediction error by up to 34% at extreme angles of attack and about 15% on average.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate flux discretization and may require careful implementation to remain stable and effective across different grid resolutions and flow regimes.
paper_title: CoFINN: Conservation Flux Informed Neural Networks for Physics Problems Governed by Conservation Laws
